logline: A journey from a quiet rented room to St Giles’ great east window, then onward to London’s night skyline: looking up turns a passing visit into a way of paying attention.
theme: Looking up: attention changes the scale of a place.

acts.name: I — The room
acts.beat: A quiet rented room becomes a starting point; a small pause before the city.

acts.name: II — The city and the cathedral
acts.beat: The Royal Mile leads into St Giles’, where paintings, glass, and the vault draw the gaze upward.

acts.name: III — The view stays with me
acts.beat: London’s skyline carries that upward pull into the night.

lines.text: Edinburgh began with me looking up. Even this ceiling felt like a beginning.
The chair gave me somewhere to land. I could sit still before heading back out.
Old Town Chambers is at 329 High Street on Edinburgh’s Royal Mile. I stopped there with my companion among flowers and bicycles.
The Royal Mile runs about a Scots mile between Edinburgh Castle and the Palace of Holyroodhouse. We kept walking.
The street fell behind us as we stepped inside St Giles’.
The church was founded by King David I in 1124. Its crown steeple probably dates from around 1500, though the exact date is uncertain.
John Knox became minister here in 1559 and led the Protestant Reformation. Today it is a Presbyterian High Kirk; for a time in the seventeenth century, it was a cathedral.
The great east window sits at the east end of the choir. It shows the Crucifixion and the Ascension.
A guide credits the window to Ballantine of Edinburgh. Its 1874–77 inscription dates mark Falshaw’s term as Lord Provost.
The choir ceiling was decorated in 1875–76; some painted details are hard to see. Robert Lorimer designed the Thistle Chapel, added in 1910.
In 2025, St Giles’ hosted John Bellany’s 1965 painting The Box Meeting. Bellany grew up in Port Seton; its fishing life shaped his boats, fishermen, and harbour scenes.
From the Thames riverside, I found the Walkie-Talkie: Rafael Viñoly’s 155-metre tower, completed in 2014. Its upper floors hold the public Sky Garden.
